content: 1. Willett WC, Manson JE, Speizer FE, and Hu FB conducted a study on the relationship between smoking and mortality in women with type 2 diabetes, as part of the Nurses' Health Study cohort. The findings were published in Diabetes Care in December 2001 (24(12):2043-8). 2. Osganian SK, Stampfer MJ, Rimm E, Spiegelman D, Hu FB, Manson JE, and Willett WC investigated the association between vitamin C intake and the risk of coronary heart disease in women. Their research was published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology on July 16, 2003 (42(2):246-52). 3. Osganian SK, Stampfer MJ, Rimm E, Spiegelman D, Manson JE, and Willett WC examined the impact of dietary carotenoids on the risk of coronary artery disease in women. This study appeared in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in June 2003 (77(6):1390-9). 4. Jiang R, Hu FB, Giovannucci EL, Rimm EB, Stampfer MJ, Spiegelman D, Rosner BA, and Willett WC explored the joint effects of alcohol and folate intake on the risk of major chronic diseases in women. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Epidemiology on October 15, 2003 (158(8):760-71). 5. Liu S, Willett WC, Manson JE, Hu FB, Rosner B, and Colditz G studied the relationship between changes in dietary fiber and grain product intake and changes in weight and obesity development among middle-aged women. This research was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in November 2003 (78(5):920-7). 6. Hu FB provided an overview of the role of plant-based foods in the prevention of cardiovascular disease. This review was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in September 2003 (78(3 Suppl):544S-551S). 7. Knight EL, Stampfer MJ, Rimm EB, Hankinson SE, and Curhan GC conducted a prospective study on moderate alcohol intake and its association with renal function decline in women. The study was published in Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation in August 2003 (18(8):1549-54). 8. Tanasescu M, Cho E, Manson JE, and Hu FB examined the relationship between dietary fat and cholesterol intake and the risk of cardiovascular disease in women with type 2 diabetes. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in June 2004 (79(6):999-1005). 9. Cannuscio CC, Colditz GA, Rimm EB, Berkman LF, Jones CP, and Kawachi I studied the effects of employment status and social ties on caregivers' mental health. This research was published in Social Science & Medicine in April 2004 (58(7):1247-56). 10. Mozaffarian D, Pischon T, Hankinson SE, Rifai N, Joshipura K, Willett WC, and Rimm EB investigated the association between dietary intake of trans fatty acids and systemic inflammation in women. Their study was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in April 2004 (79(4):606-12). 11. Rich-Edwards JW, Stampfer MJ, Manson JE, Rosner B, Hu FB, Michels KB, and Willett WC explored the relationship between breastfeeding during infancy and the risk of cardiovascular disease in adulthood. This study appeared in Epidemiology in September 2004 (15(5):550-6). 12. Weinstein AR, Sesso HD, Lee IM, Cook NR, Manson JE, Buring JE, and Gaziano JM examined the relationship between physical activity and body mass index in relation to type 2 diabetes risk in women. Their findings were published in JAMA on September 8, 2004 (292(10):1188-94). 13. Pai JK, Pischon T, Ma J, Manson JE, Hankinson SE, Joshipura K, Curhan GC, Rifai N, Cannuscio CC, Stampfer MJ, and Rimm EB studied inflammatory markers and their association with the risk of coronary heart disease in men and women. This research was published in the New England Journal of Medicine on December 16, 2004 (351(25):2599-610). 14. Oh K, Hu FB, Cho E, Rexrode KM, Stampfer MJ, Manson JE, Liu S, and Willett WC investigated the relationship between carbohydrate intake, glycemic index, glycemic load, and dietary fiber with the risk of stroke in women. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Epidemiology on January 15, 2005 (161(2):161-9). 15. Hu FB, Willett WC, Li T, Stampfer MJ, Colditz GA, and Manson JE compared the predictive value of adiposity and physical activity for mortality among women. This study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine on December 23, 2004 (351(26):2694-703). 16. Albert CM, Chae CU, Rexrode KM, Manson JE, and Kawachi I examined the association between phobic anxiety and the risk of coronary heart disease and sudden cardiac death in women. Their research was published in Circulation on February 1, 2005 (111(4):480-7). 17. Schulze MB, Shai I, Manson JE, Li T, Rifai N, Jiang R, and Hu FB studied the combined role of non-HDL cholesterol and glycated hemoglobin in predicting future coronary heart disease events among women with type 2 diabetes. This study was published in Diabetologia in December 2004 (47(12):2129-36). 18. Erkkilä AT, Booth SL, Hu FB, Jacques PF, Manson JE, Rexrode KM, Stampfer MJ, and Lichtenstein AH investigated phylloquinone intake as a marker for coronary heart disease risk but not stroke in women. Their findings were published in the European Journal of Clinical Nutrition in February 2005 (59(2):196-204). 19. Al-Delaimy WK, Rexrode KM, Hu FB, Albert CM, Stampfer MJ, Willett WC, and Manson JE studied the relationship between folate intake and the risk of stroke in women. This research was published in Stroke in June 2004 (35(6):1259-63). 20. Forman JP, Rimm EB, Stampfer MJ, and Curhan GC examined the association between folate intake and the risk of developing hypertension among U.S. women. Their findings were published in JAMA on January 19, 2005 (293(3):320-9). 21. Oh K, Hu FB, Manson JE, Stampfer MJ, and Willett WC analyzed the relationship between dietary fat intake and the risk of coronary heart disease in women over 20 years of follow-up in the Nurses' Health Study. This study was published in the American Journal of Epidemiology on April 1, 2005 (161(7):672-9). 22. Shai I, Schulze MB, Manson JE, Rexrode KM, Stampfer MJ, Mantzoros C, and Hu FB conducted a prospective study on soluble tumor necrosis factor-alpha receptor II (sTNF-RII) and its association with coronary heart disease risk among women with type 2 diabetes. Their findings were published in Diabetes Care in June 2005 (28(6):1376-82). 23. Mukamal KJ, Jensen MK, Gronbaek M, Stampfer MJ, Manson JE, Pischon T, and Rimm EB studied the relationship between drinking frequency, mediating biomarkers, and the risk of myocardial infarction in women and men. This research was published in Circulation on September 6, 2005 (112(10):1406-13). 24. Pai JK, Kraft P, Cannuscio CC, Manson JE, Rexrode KM, Albert CM, Hunter D, and Rimm EB investigated polymorphisms in the CC-chemokine receptor-2 (CCR2) and -5 (CCR5) genes and their association with coronary heart disease risk among U.S. women. Their findings were published in Atherosclerosis in July 2005. 25. Rich-Edwards JW, Kleinman K, Michels KB, Stampfer MJ, Manson JE, Rexrode KM, Hiber EN, and Willett WC conducted a longitudinal study on birth weight and adult body mass index in predicting the risk of coronary heart disease and stroke in women. This study was published in BMJ on May 14, 2005 (330(7500):1115). 26. Albert CM, Oh K, Whang W, Manson JE, Chae CU, Stampfer MJ, Willett WC, and Hu FB examined the relationship between dietary alpha-linolenic acid intake and the risk of sudden cardiac death and coronary heart disease. Their findings were published in Circulation on November 22, 2005 (112(21):3232-8).
